headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-chaining between Flowise and mem0 can leak data and amplify errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, so attacker-controlled content can enter its flows; mem0 is a knowledge store that may later surface stored text back into prompts. No explicit shared channel is documented, so this is an inferred interaction and uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF Flowise ingests untrusted files or web pages into a flow that later feeds mem0-stored text back into prompts
IF mem0 returns stored content to Flowise without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for sources entering Flowise flows
Strip instructions from retrieved mem0 memories before reuse
Tag retrieved content with provenance and trust level
Review any browser/tool node outputs before passing them onward

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and model/tool credentials, while mem0 is a memory layer with no declared egress. A shared workspace or datastore path could expose sensitive chatflow data to memory storage or retrieval. Because the pairwise data path is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Flowise stores uploaded files or chatflow outputs in a location mem0 can read
IF mem0 persists sensitive memories from Flowise conversations
mitigations: Separate storage locations for Flowise and mem0
Disable memory writes for sensitive chatflows
Redact secrets before any memory insertion
Audit shared datastore permissions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has broad filesystem write and server-datastore shared state across instances; mem0 has no declared write surface, but it is a mutable memory system by category. The overlap is not proven, yet shared mutable state makes write conflicts plausible in default deployments, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both systems write to the same backing store or directory
IF Flowise instances and mem0 workers mutate shared records without locking
mitigations: Use separate backing stores
Enable per-record locking or optimistic concurrency checks
Restrict Flowise write paths to a dedicated directory
Schedule writes to avoid concurrent mutation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise can emit tool and model outputs that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, and mem0 is a memory/knowledge component that may re-inject those outputs later. If mem0 stores unverified Flowise output, later retrieval can amplify a single mistake across sessions. The interaction is plausible but undocumented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Flowise-generated facts or summaries without verification
IF later Flowise runs consume those memories as authoritative context
mitigations: Require human review before persisting memories
Store source links alongside each memory
Add a verification step before acting on retrieved memories
Limit memory reuse to non-authoritative hints

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise explicitly handles model provider keys, tool credentials, and chatflow inputs/outputs, while mem0’s profile does not declare regulated-data handling or residency constraints. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Flowise chatflows and then persisted into mem0
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls that mem0 does not document
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in memories
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Mask secrets before persistence
Confirm residency requirements before deployment
